addProblem.problemIdHint: Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only

addProblem.solutionTemplatesHint: Optionally provide reference solutions for the problem.

aiGenerator.title: AI Problem Generator
aiGenerator.subtitle: Describe the type of coding problem you want to practice. The AI will generate a custom algorithm problem for you.
aiGenerator.requestPlaceholder: e.g., I want to do a dynamic programming problem, or I want to do a string processing problem
aiGenerator.instruction1: Describe the type of problem you want (algorithm type, difficulty, topic)
aiGenerator.instruction2: You can write in English or Chinese
aiGenerator.instruction3: Be specific about what you want to practice (e.g., "dynamic programming", "graph algorithms")
aiGenerator.instruction4: The AI will generate a complete problem with test cases and solutions
aiGenerator.instruction5: The generated problem will be automatically added to your problem collection
aiGenerator.noAIProviderConfigured: No AI provider is configured. Please configure one of the supported AI providers in your environment variables.
aiGenerator.jsonParseError: Failed to parse the generated JSON. You can fix it in the editor below.
aiGenerator.fixJsonInstructions: The AI generated content that couldn't be parsed as valid JSON. Please fix any syntax errors and save the corrected JSON.
aiGenerator.invalidJsonFormat: Invalid JSON format. Please check for syntax errors.

manage.title: Manage Problems
manage.importFromFolderDescription: Load all JSON files from a local folder. Each JSON file can contain a single problem or an array of problems.
manage.problemsFolderHint: Load all JSON files from the 'problems' folder in the application directory
manage.customFolderHint: Enter the full path to a folder containing JSON problem files
manage.importDescription: Enter one or more URLs to JSON files containing problems. Each URL should point to an array of problem objects. You can enter multiple URLs, one per line.
manage.multiUrlHint: Enter one URL per line to import from multiple sources
manage.jsonFormatDescription: JSON files should contain an array of problem objects (or a single problem object) with the following structure:
manage.deleteConfirmMessage: Are you sure you want to delete {{count}} problem(s)? This action cannot be undone.

list.title: Engineering Practice
list.entryHint: Move from puzzles to systems: a real multi-file workspace, stage-by-stage builds, reviewed on concurrency, latency, encapsulation and elegance.
list.heading: Engineering projects
list.subtitle: Each project is a small system you build in stages. You work in a full multi-file workspace, and the hidden acceptance specs check more than correctness, they gate on engineering metrics like concurrency and latency.

stage.label: Stage {{current}}/{{total}}
stage.locked: Clear the previous stage to unlock
stage.referenceLocked: Clear this stage to see the reference implementation
stage.pitfallsHint: These pass some specs but are wrong as engineering

workspace.readonlyHint: Contract file provided by the platform, read only
workspace.noFileOpen: Pick a file on the left to start
workspace.editedHint: This file differs from the stage starter. Click to see the diff. Your edits are saved automatically.
workspace.languageHint: Switching swaps the starter files and specs; each language keeps its own drafts

metrics.timelineHint: Virtual time on the x-axis, in-flight requests on the y-axis, a sequential implementation is a flat line at 1.

review.title: AI engineering review
review.subtitle: Reviewed like a pull request: concurrency safety, failure behaviour, module boundaries, abstractions
review.empty: Ask AI to review the workspace the way a staff engineer would. It sees your code, the latest run and the static analysis metrics.

chat.title: Engineering assistant
chat.empty: I can see your workspace code, the stage goal and your latest run. Ask about approach, failures or design trade-offs.
chat.placeholder: Ask about the current implementation… (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a newline)

prompts.metrics: Why are my concurrency/latency gates failing?
prompts.howToStart: Where should I start this stage?
prompts.design: What design options do I have?

generator.title: Generate a project
generator.heading: Generate an engineering project
generator.subtitle: Describe the engineering skill you want to drill. AI designs a staged, multi-file project with hidden specs, metric gates and a reference solution.
generator.requestLabel: What do you want to practise
generator.requestHint: Be specific: the kind of system, and the engineering concern you want tested (concurrency, caching, resilience, boundaries…)
generator.placeholder: e.g. a log batching uploader with backpressure, batching and drop policy
generator.verifyNote: The platform runs the reference solution to verify the generated project before saving it
generator.loadingHint: Generating and verifying: design stages → write specs → execute the reference solution → repair. This usually takes 1-3 minutes.
generator.problemsTitle: Problems found while executing this project
generator.noDiscrimination: the starter skeleton also passes, specs lack discrimination
